blindFormulaPacket.surfactantArchitecture: Primary anionic alkyl ether sulfate (Sodium Laureth Sulfate #2) buffered by amphoteric Cocamidopropyl Betaine #3 and mild nonionic Coco-Glucoside #7; no second anionic, no reset/chelating route. Sodium Chloride #4 is a thickener.
blindFormulaPacket.conditioningDepositionRoutes: One cationic guar (Hydroxypropyl Guar Hydroxypropyltrimonium Chloride #11, listed after Bisabolol #10, i.e. low level); refatter Glyceryl Oleate #6; Hydrogenated Vegetable Glycerides Citrate #13 (minor emulsifier/refatter). No silicone, no fatty alcohol, no oil, no protein, no pearlizer.
blindFormulaPacket.humectantRefattingClues: Panthenol #8, Glyceryl Oleate #6, Niacinamide #9; no Glycerin.
blindFormulaPacket.scalpActives: Piroctone Olamine #5 (recognized anti-dandruff active); comfort routes Panthenol #8, Niacinamide #9, Bisabolol #10; Sodium Salicylate #14 (preservative-range salt, not a counted active).
blindFormulaPacket.exposureFlags: No Parfum, no essential oil, no menthol/cooling agent. Preservative Sodium Benzoate #17 (+ Sodium Salicylate #14).

cleansingStrength.rationale: Moderate: an early SLES chassis buffered by a betaine and a glucoside, with no second anionic or reset route, is exactly the C1 pattern.
cleansingStrength.counterSignals: SLES is the dominant surfactant and is a genuine strong-cleansing clue; the formula is not a mild amino-acid/glucoside-led system, so it is not 'low' despite the sensitive positioning.

conditioningLevel.rationale: Low: cleansing-led formula whose only hair-substantive route is a low-level cationic guar; the refatter and panthenol add feel, not meaningful slip.

formulaFacts.role: cationic polymer, after Bisabolol #10 so plausibly low level

ruleIds: C2 (not triggered: no silicone, no pearlizer/fatty route)
conditioningLevel.counterSignals: A cationic guar plus a refatter plus panthenol could be read as 'several light routes' = moderate; guar position and absence of silicone/fatty alcohol argue for low.

weightPotential.rationale: Low: one light, late cationic guar and a weak refatter in an effective SLES/betaine base; no silicone, oil, wax or rich 2-in-1 architecture.

subjudgments.whyThisBand: Anchor text: 'One light polymer, weak refatter ... can remain low'. That is the whole deposition story here.
subjudgments.whyNotNeighborBand: Moderate needs one meaningfully persistent system or interacting routes; there is no silicone, amodimethicone, oil payload, fatty alcohol or second cationic route.

weightPotential.counterSignals: Cationic guar is a deposition clue (not a moderate floor).
weightPotential.neighborNote: No realistic INCI-only unknown moves this to moderate; recorded as none. A lane that records 'moderate' as neighbour would raise review_thickness_boundary for fine (T4).

focusPrimary.decisionTrace: Formula: recognized anti-dandruff active plus comfort routes in a moderate SLES/betaine chassis. Claim: name and front pack say Anti Schuppen, 'stark & nachhaltig gegen Schuppen'. Counter-signal (sensitive/mild wording) is absorbed into scalp_active per Appendix A (Vichy Dercos Sensitiv precedent). No competing specialist focus.

focusSecondary.counterSignals: Panthenol/Niacinamide headline could be read as a moisture claim, but it is not a hair-length claim and shares the scalp-comfort route.

scalpTargets.secondaryRationale: No secondary. Sensitive: E2 requires a claim naming a scalp condition ('sensible/empfindliche Kopfhaut', 'Juckreiz', 'beruhigt die Kopfhaut'); this product says 'Ultra Sensitiv+' (no scalp named), 'sehr sensible Haut' (range-level boilerplate, E1 excludes) and 'sanft zur Kopfhaut' ('sanft' is listed as non-qualifying). The formula gate would pass (targeted + prominent Panthenol #8 / Niacinamide #9 / Bisabolol #10 before Sodium Salicylate #14, E3/E4), but the positioning gate does not, so P0 keeps it off. No S-FAIL: no E2 sensitive claim was made. Dry: no dry-scalp claim. Oily: none.

customerFit.separationNote: Section 15: this is user fit, derived separately; it does not change any property or projection value.
customerFit.customer: Viola: wavy, fine strands, high density, medium length, colored + bleached, elastic test snaps, dry scalp; June 2026 reported dry flakes ('trockene Schuppen'); Oct 3 quiz: no scalp problems. Main issues: dry lengths, frizz, tangling, low shine, lost wave. Routine: this shampoo ~1x/week -> Syoss Intense Glaze lamination mask as conditioner -> Neqi leave-in mist -> Neqi Opulent Oil.
customerFit.verdictSummary: Fine to keep for now; switch to a fragrance-free everyday shampoo for dry/sensitive scalp once the flakes have stayed away. Either way the shampoo is not what is driving her dry, snapping lengths.

reasons.assessment: Good fit. Low weight potential means it will not weigh down fine, wavy hair (fine = ideal under T1).

reasons.topic: Anti-dandruff active vs her actual flakes
reasons.assessment: Piroctone olamine is made for classic dandruff. She described dry flakes, and our standard treats dry flakes as a dry-scalp comfort issue, not automatically dandruff. With no scalp complaints in October she does not clearly need the active any more. It does no obvious harm at 1x/week, and her current once-a-week use already works like a maintenance rhythm. If her flakes only stayed away because of this shampoo, that is a reason to keep it.

reasons.topic: Cleansing strength on bleached, snapping hair
reasons.assessment: Moderate cleansing with an SLES base, buffered by betaine and glucoside, so it is not harsh. It is also not the mildest option for very damaged hair. At once a week with a mask afterwards, exposure is low. Weekly washing of dense hair carrying leave-in plus oil needs real cleansing, so a very weak shampoo could leave residue. Practical lever: lather on the scalp only and let the rinse run through the lengths.
Supportive. No perfume, no menthol, panthenol, niacinamide and bisabolol, and a refatter. This is a sensible pick for a dry, easily irritated scalp.
Low conditioning: the shampoo contributes nothing to dry lengths, frizz or tangling. Her mask, leave-in and oil carry that job, so a swap here will not fix the lengths.

Under the v1.6 projection the product would sit only in the fine/normal x dandruff group. With a dry scalp and no current complaint, she would normally be matched to the dry-scalp group, which this product does not serve. That supports 'switch once flakes are gone' rather than 'keep forever'.

callQuestions: Are the flakes completely gone, and did they come back when you used a different shampoo? What did they look like: fine, white and dry with a tight feeling, or larger, yellowish and itchy?
How does your scalp feel 3-6 days after washing: tight or itchy, or fine? Do you lather your lengths too, or only the scalp?
Right after shampooing, before the mask, do your lengths feel squeaky or rough? Do you use any other shampoo in between?
customerFit.boundary: Cosmetic guidance only. If flakes return strongly, or the scalp becomes red, sore or very itchy, suggest she ask a pharmacist or doctor.
customerFit.swapDirectionIfNeeded: A fragrance-free, mild everyday shampoo positioned for dry or sensitive scalp, with a humectant or refatter, without anti-dandruff active, and light enough for fine hair (W low). The same line's 'ISANA MED Shampoo Jeden Tag (Ultra Sensitiv)' (EAN 4305615629223: 0% perfume, Glycerin #3, Panthenol, Allantoin, no anti-dandruff active) is an obvious candidate to check, but it has NOT been classified here.

openIssues: Process: single lane, not blind (claims visible from the brief). Needs a second sealed lane before any use under the v1.6 lock process.

Standard gap (E2 lexicon): 'Ultra Sensitiv+' in the product name plus 'sanft zur Kopfhaut' does not qualify as a sensitive-scalp claim, so no secondary sensitive target (irritationen/irritated). If Nick rules that a 'Sensitiv' product name on a shampoo counts as a scalp claim, fine+normal x irritationen/irritated/regular rows would be added (supportive, because that bucket expects gentle). Direction: toward_recommending, so the conservative value is kept.
